uncertainties.note: The stored answer follows the copied exam option that BCC diffusion is faster because of a larger number of interstitial sites. This is acceptable in the professor-style option set, but the wording says "Fe atom" rather than an interstitial atom such as C; strictly, Fe self-diffusion is not interstitial diffusion.

The keyed answer D is the clearest Hume-Rothery trap because a large electronegativity difference favors compounds rather than extensive solid solution. However, option B (interstitials) is also not normally a condition for extensive substitutional solubility, so the original past-exam wording is somewhat ambiguous.

The intended answer B is supported by anisotropy of thermal expansion. Option D (thermal expansion coefficient "measures the softness of crystals") is also scientifically loose unless interpreted through the course's Condon-Morse/bond-softness discussion.

The intended answer D is reasonable because pure metals are not generally stiffer than alloys. Option B (pure metals are more corrosion resistant) is composition- and environment-dependent, so the original NOT-style wording is not fully clean.

The keyed answer A (steel alloying) is the clearly wrong limestone function. The distractor "prevent oxidation of pig iron" is only defensible if interpreted as slag/cover protection; limestone's primary course role is fluxing impurities into slag and lowering the effective melting behavior of the charge.
